chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in his will to his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah:

Beware of haughtiness, ill-temper, and lack of patience, for with these three characteristics, no companion will remain steady with you, and people will continually avoid you. Keep yourself attached to kindness, and be patient with the burdens people place on you. Give your friend your self and your wealth. Give your acquaintance your support and your presence. Give the general public your cheerfulness and your love. Give your enemy your justice and your fairness. Guard your religion and your honor from everyone, for that is safer for your religion and your worldly life.
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics to avoid and the virtues to adopt according to Imam Ali's will to his son?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) practical ethics in *Al-Khusus* (specific traits), emphasizing that social cohesion depends on mastering self-restraint and reciprocal generosity. The advice to 'guard your religion and honor' reflects the Shia concept of *Hifz al-Din* through social conduct, ensuring that one’s public interactions do not compromise spiritual integrity or communal standing.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-178 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Isa quoted Hammad ibn Isa, who linked it up through other narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that in his will to his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanifeh, the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said,

“I admonish you against haughtiness, ill temperedness and impatience since then you will have no friends and everyone will avoid you. Try to be kind with people and be patient with the losses which the people make you suffer. Be generous with your friends regarding yourself and your wealth. Accept the company of your friends and associate with them. Be warm and kind to the general public. Treat your enemy justly. Protect your religion and honor. This is much better for your religion and worldly life.”
